fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Earth Pipes Across Arizona", "body": "Mitch describes his Earth Pipes Across Arizona project, in which he and friends bury or grid orgonite devices sealed inside metal pipes around cell towers and other high EMF points, a practice he calls gifting. Tallying his receipts the night before with a friend's help, he finds the count is just shy of 800 pipes since his last appearance, built mostly in his garage over about two months. His advice is to start in your own yard and let neighbors spread it outward. Chance reads a viewer comment from someone inspired to start making her own pieces."}, {"title": "Monsoon Season and the Receipts", "body": "Mitch says Arizona is finally having a real monsoon after none last year and a pitiful one before that, and he credits his gifting rather than chance. On screen he compares Phoenix weather from a month earlier, when he cites highs up to 118, against current highs near 104 and a July day around 94. He also recounts fire smoke near Payson and Flagstaff fading after the last radar tower there was gifted, with warning signs downgraded. These are his readings of events, offered as receipts he wants to document."}, {"title": "Headlines With No Winning Move", "body": "Mitch calls the climate crisis the end game boogeyman, following what he describes as a lockdown training ground, and challenges listeners to search climate crisis hashtags and read the five most dramatic headlines in full. He dissects one claiming over a billion seashore animals were cooked in British Columbia, saying the evidence was a few thousand deaths in a polluted canal. Both men say the media frames every kind of weather as catastrophe, from a weak monsoon to flash floods and burn scars, and Chance adds that even alternative media can become doom scroll fear porn."}, {"title": "Feeding the Web With Attention", "body": "Both men tie outcomes to attention. Mitch says sharing alarming articles without context only feeds the web, citing a California follower who constantly complains about fires, and he holds that thoughts become things and that anyone gifting needs top-notch energy. Chance asks why we circulate what we do, hoping it is constructive, uplifting or at least funny, and later argues that respecting free will and growing aware of interconnection offers a kind of shielding, while allowing that agreements made before birth may complicate any promise of safety."}, {"title": "Packages, Pushback and the Frequency Fence", "body": "Mitch tells how a box of orgonite bound for the Georgia Guidestones detoured through Anchorage and arrived a day late, which Chance notes is near HAARP. Mitch laughs it off as pushback and says he had already mailed others. Chance frames the frequency fence as a medium that any spraying would ride on, and Mitch replies that he no longer subscribes to the aluminum, barium and strontium story, preferring to call the trails energy field reactions. He closes by teasing a larger project beyond Arizona and a Restore the Desert page on his website."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Mitch Kohl is back to give us some updates on how his orgone device gifting quests have impacted Arizona this summer.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "A Bigger Boogeyman From NASA", "body": "Back from the break, Mitch reads headlines in which NASA warns of coastal flooding within a decade because of a wobbling moon, and he predicts the next scare will be water now that, in his view, the geoengineering is being undone. He recalls a Crow 777 episode claiming Hubble telemetry is fake and says he trusts NASA warnings little. Chance stays open about Atlantis or Tartaria without pinning everything on either, argues something clearly happened because modern buildings are so poorly made, and asks whether fifty proven lies justify doubting the rest."}, {"title": "Can Anyone Really Make It Rain", "body": "Mitch says friends in Texas who gift orgonite report a wet, drought-free year and that early drought and heat wave articles were pulled, while Chance notes cloud seeding has long been used to make snow near ski resorts. Mitch counters that silver iodide barely boosts precipitation and concludes nobody can truly make it rain; in his view gifting restores the natural life energy field so weather goes where it needs to go. Chance reads orgone as the universe's intent and deadly orgone radiation as its stoppage, which Mitch sharpens into life versus its absence."}, {"title": "Pyramids, Seeds and a Booming Garden", "body": "Mitch describes Alexander Golod's 150 foot pyramids outside Moscow, which he says sharpened blades, refined underground oil and brought extinct plants back, and he reads this as life energy pulling genetic code into being. Chance wonders aloud about spontaneous generation and why dormant seeds germinate when they do. Mitch offers his garden as evidence: a heat wave ended last year's attempt, while this year strawberries, sunflowers, oregano and basil exploded within days of the first big June monsoon, which he credits to rain he calls supercharged, structured water pulled from the ether."}, {"title": "Mechanistic Minds and Mystical Minds", "body": "Chance reads a Reich passage from Ether, God and Devil and summarizes Reich's view that people swing between mechanistic and mystical thinking, both detached from felt reality. Mitch says he tries to find the middle ground, objects that orgone gets lumped in with the New Age, and favors practical steps such as burying an earth pipe or removing a smart meter or Wi Fi. He shows an experimental life meter he uses on soil and plants. Mitch cites Reich's line that nobody must prove anything to anyone, and Chance ties it to learning through sensation and feeling."}, {"title": "Practical Tricks and What We Are Allowed to Say", "body": "Mitch offers tips for city gifters, from dropping orgonite in cardboard tubes into hollow fence posts to grinding in earth pipes with a drill bit, and urges starting at home, as he did by supplying his UPS driver and a grocery store worker. He demonstrates an ether damming pipe, which he says can break up stalled storm cells and electrosmog, and says he leans away from the aluminum, barium and strontium story. Chance suggests small cells of friends, though both distrust big movements. Mitch closes asking what ideas are allowed to spread."}]

We did not have one last year and we had a pitiful one the year before that.", "author": "Mitch The Orgone Donor", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/8fa8a281-e0d6-4525-a649-03a65d1b17da/MITCH-THE-ORGONE-DONOR.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Just like every other form of weather that is ever reported on by mainstream media, whatever it is, it is the worst, most apocalyptic, end of the world terrible thing imaginable.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "So help me God, I will make sure that everyone in Arizona who wants one has an earth pipe.", "author": "Mitch The Orgone Donor", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/8fa8a281-e0d6-4525-a649-03a65d1b17da/MITCH-THE-ORGONE-DONOR.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Even a lot of what you call alternative media sources are not much better than sort of doom scroll fear porn outlets as well.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "We live in a world where people can't fathom that somebody would want to harm them. And that's one of our biggest crutches as a species.", "author": "Mitch The Orgone Donor", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/8fa8a281-e0d6-4525-a649-03a65d1b17da/MITCH-THE-ORGONE-DONOR.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Once we reach a certain level of awareness of the interconnectedness of everything, I do think that it develops a strong amount of shielding or invulnerability to being screwed with.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "When they say we're your weather authority on the screen, if you participate in that crap, they are in fact your weather authority.", "author": "Mitch The Orgone Donor", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/8fa8a281-e0d6-4525-a649-03a65d1b17da/MITCH-THE-ORGONE-DONOR.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "All of this fake climate push that they put out there, we're manifesting it if we fall for it.", "author": "Mitch The Orgone Donor", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/8fa8a281-e0d6-4525-a649-03a65d1b17da/MITCH-THE-ORGONE-DONOR.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}]
